next_step: Finalize Dedicated sizing + pricing; turn in security questionnaire; exec review
notes:
Summary: Mid-market product company building a conversational product for SMB customers. Originally on incumbent LLM API; experiencing sustained latency regressions over last 2 quarters -> exploring migration. Primary evaluation path: hosted API POC (streaming + tool calling) -> sizing/pricing conversation for Dedicated reserved pool if POC meets SLOs.

Key requirements (customer language):
- "fast feel" chat for agents: start-of-response <100ms, end-to-end P95 <500ms for short replies, sustained 80-150 RPS across peak windows.
- Robust streaming + tool-calling (external API orchestration) w/ deterministic token streaming and graceful fallbacks.
- Moderate cost sensitivity; want predictable pricing for peak season.
- Compliance: SOC2 required, SSO (SAML) + audit logs + ability to keep EU data in region (future).

Timeline (high level):
- 2024-09-03: Inbound interest (support forum + growth outreach). Account created.
- 2024-09-15: Discovery call (Jordan Blake) — discussed migration pains, incumbent latency regressions, desire to benchmark streaming.
- 2024-10-02: Hosted demo — streaming + function-calling walkthrough. Customer liked streaming startup latency vs incumbent.
- 2024-11-12: POC kickoff (sandbox keys issued). Built simulation harness that replays production traffic for 72h. Linked ticket POC-8792.
- 2024-12-05: First benchmark run vs incumbent (incumbent = vendor X). Notable delta; Redwood streaming shows lower start-of-stream and lower P95 under steady load.
- 2025-01-15: Review meeting (FR = ff-03b9a7) — internal tech + PM + infra present. Shared Drive: pricing + security docs.

POC / Benchmark details (customer-visible highlights):
- Harness: production replay (typical session 12 tokens avg before tool call). 20 concurrent workers to simulate peak.
- Targets: median start-of-stream <120ms, P95 token step <300ms, end-to-end P95 <500ms, sustain 100 RPS with <1% tail error.
- Redwood (hosted API, streaming enabled) results: median start-of-stream ~80ms; P95 token-step ~210ms; sustained 120 RPS with CPU/GPU autoscaling; tool-calling success 96%; end-to-end P95 for short replies ~340ms.
- Incumbent results: median start-of-stream ~320ms; P95 token-step ~890ms; sustained 60 RPS before errors rose; tool-calling 92% with higher retry rate.
- Notes: Redwood's prefix/KV caching reduced repeated-token cost significantly in replay; continuous batching helped throughput. Incumbent had intermittent latency regressions during bursts (customer cited 2 incidents in last 8 weeks).

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "Users notice the lag — it's our churn lever." (PM)
- "If we can standardize latency and avoid surprises, we can move to a reserved pool." (CTO)

Commercial / pricing convo:
- Redwood provided hosted pricing vs estimated Dedicated baseline (Reserved GPU pool) — initial Dedicated estimate ~$12k/mo for baseline capacity (sustaining up to 150 RPS with reserved buffers). Hosted per-token pricing used for POC numbers; customer asked for 3x scale footprint pricing + burst policy.
- Customer sensitive to long-term unit cost; asked for recommendations (Optimize team) re: batching + quantization profiles.

Risks and open items:
- Need full SOC2 package and EU data residency commitment language (legal).
- Edge case: multi-tool orchestration path caused 4% higher latency in one workflow; engineering investigating optimizer/runtime config.
- Procurement timeline targets Q2 purchasing window — may delay Dedicated close.

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood: share Dedicated sizing + firm pricing for 3 scale tiers (Priya lead). Provide SOC2 artifact bundle and KMS/DR flow. Share Optimize recommendations for lower unit cost.
- Customer: run one more 72h replay with Canaries enabled (tool-call orchestration tweaks), internal exec review week of 2025-02-05, legal to review residency language.
- Follow-up meeting scheduled 2025-02-12 (prep: updated benchmark report + Dedicated quote).

CRM style quick notes / fragments:
- POC shows clear perf delta vs incumbent — primary migration driver = latency.
- Sales angle: sell predictability (reserved capacity) + migration assistance.
- Tech ask: SLOs for streaming + replay harness reproducibility.
- Blocker: legal residency + procurement timing.
